claim: Many 3D structures of cation-coupled transporters have been determined, but the mechanistic details governing the obligatory coupling and functional regulations still remain elusive.
source: While many 3D structures of cation-coupled transporters have been determined, the mechanistic details governing the obligatory coupling and functional regulations still remain elusive.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field, supported by the context of the manuscript.

claim: The bacterial melibiose transporter (MelB) is a prototype of major facilitator superfamily transporters.
source: The bacterial melibiose transporter (MelB) is a prototype of major facilitator superfamily transporters.
evidence: This is a classification statement supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: A low-sugar affinity inward-facing Na+-bound cryoEM structure was determined using a conformation-selective nanobody.
source: With a conformation-selective nanobody, we determined a low-sugar affinity inward-facing Na+-bound cryoEM structure.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The N- and C-terminal residues of the inner barrier contribute to the sugar selectivity in the outward-facing sugar-bound structures.
source: The available outward-facing sugar-bound structures showed that the N- and C-terminal residues of the inner barrier contribute to the sugar selectivity.
evidence: This is supported by structural data from previously determined structures.

claim: The sugar selectivity pocket is broken when the inner barrier is broken in the inward-open conformation.
source: The inward-open conformation shows that the sugar selectivity pocket is also broken when the inner barrier is broken.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM structure determined in this study.

claim: The inward-facing conformation trapped by the nanobody exhibited a greatly decreased sugar-binding affinity.
source: Isothermal titration calorimetry measurements revealed that this inward-facing conformation trapped by this nanobody exhibited a greatly decreased sugar-binding affinity, suggesting the mechanisms for substrate intracellular release and accumulation.
evidence: This is supported by ITC measurements presented in the manuscript.

claim: The inner/outer barrier shift directly regulates the sugar-binding affinity.
source: While the inner/outer barrier shift directly regulates the sugar-binding affinity, it has little or no effect on the cation binding, which is supported by molecular dynamics simulations.
evidence: This is supported by both experimental data and MD simulations.

claim: The inner/outer barrier shift has little or no effect on the cation binding.
source: While the inner/outer barrier shift directly regulates the sugar-binding affinity, it has little or no effect on the cation binding, which is supported by molecular dynamics simulations.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: HDX-MS analyses identified dynamic regions involved in the functionally important inner barrier-specific salt-bridge network.
source: Furthermore, the hydron/deuterium exchange mass spectrometry analyses allowed us to identify dynamic regions; some regions are involved in the functionally important inner barrier-specific salt-bridge network, which indicates their critical roles in the barrier switching mechanisms for transport.
evidence: This is supported by HDX-MS experimental data.

claim: Cation-coupled transporters play critical roles in many aspects of cell physiology and pharmacokinetics.
source: Cation-coupled transporters play critical roles in many aspects of cell physiology and pharmacokinetics and are involved in many serious diseases, including cancers, metabolic diseases, neurodegenerative diseases, etc.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: Cation-coupled transporters are involved in many serious diseases, including cancers, metabolic diseases, and neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Cation-coupled transporters play critical roles in many aspects of cell physiology and pharmacokinetics and are involved in many serious diseases, including cancers, metabolic diseases, neurodegenerative diseases, etc.
evidence: This is supported by cited literature.

claim: The specific locations and functions of cation-coupled transporters make them viable drug targets.

evidence: This is supported by cited literature.

claim: The structures of many transporters have been determined by x-ray crystallography and cryoEM.
source: Following decades of effort, the structures of many transporters have been determined by x-ray crystallography and, more recently, by cryoEM (Abramson et al., 2003; Cherezov et al., 2007; Kumar et al., 2014; Huang et al., 2003; Boudker et al., 2007; Yamashita et al., 2005; Gouaux, 2009; Pedersen et al., 2013; Ethayathulla et al., 2014; Yan, 2015; Drew et al., 2021; Guan, 2022).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: There is still no deep understanding of the structural basis for substrate accumulation to high concentrations.
source: However, we still do not have a deep understanding of the structural basis for substrate accumulation to high concentrations, the mechanisms for the obligatorily coupled transport, as well as the cellular regulation of transporters' activities to meet metabolic needs.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium melibiose permease (MelBSt) is the prototype Na+/solute transporter of the major facilitator superfamilies (MFS).
source: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium melibiose permease (MelBSt) is the prototype Na+/solute transporter of the major facilitator superfamilies (MFS) (Ethayathulla et al., 2014; Guan, 2018; Markham et al., 2021; Hariharan and Guan, 2017; Hariharan et al., 2018; Guan and Hariharan, 2021; Blaimschein et al., 2023; Granell et al., 2010; Ganea et al., 2001; Chae et al., 2010; Panda et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: MelBSt catalyzes the stoichiometric symport of galactopyranoside with Na+, H+, or Li+.
source: It catalyzes the stoichiometric symport of galactopyranoside with Na+, H+, or Li+ (Guan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: Crystal structures of sugar-bound states of MelBSt have been determined, which reveals the sugar recognition mechanism.

evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: In all solved x-ray crystal structures, MelBSt is in an outward-facing conformation.
source: In all solved x-ray crystal structures, MelBSt is in an outward-facing conformation; the observed physical barrier of the sugar translocation, named the inner barrier, prevents the substrate from moving into the cytoplasm directly.
evidence: This is a statement about previously determined structures.

claim: The inner barrier prevents the substrate from moving into the cytoplasm directly in the outward-facing conformation.
source: In all solved x-ray crystal structures, MelBSt is in an outward-facing conformation; the observed physical barrier of the sugar translocation, named the inner barrier, prevents the substrate from moving into the cytoplasm directly.
evidence: This is an inference from structural data.

claim: Transporters change their conformation to allow the substrate translocation from one side of the membrane to the other.
source: It is well-known that transporters change their conformation to allow the substrate translocation from one side of the membrane to the other and conformational dynamics is the intrinsic feature necessary for their functions (Abramson et al., 2003; Huang et al., 2003; Boudker et al., 2007; Yan, 2015; Drew et al., 2021; Guan and Kaback, 2006; Khare et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Conformational dynamics is the intrinsic feature necessary for transporter functions.
source: It is well-known that transporters change their conformation to allow the substrate translocation from one side of the membrane to the other and conformational dynamics is the intrinsic feature necessary for their functions (Abramson et al., 2003; Huang et al., 2003; Boudker et al., 2007; Yan, 2015; Drew et al., 2021; Guan and Kaback, 2006; Khare et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Thermodynamic binding cycles in MelBSt have been established using isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) measurements.
source: To understand how the sugar substrate and the coupling cations dictate transporter function, we have established thermodynamic binding cycles in MelBSt using isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) measurements and identified that the positive cooperativity of the binding of cation and melibiose as the core symport mechanism (Hariharan and Guan, 2017); furthermore, the binding of the second substrate changes the thermodynamic feature of heat capacity change from positive to negative, suggesting primary dehydration processes when both substrates concurrently occupy the transporter (Hariharan and Guan, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The positive cooperativity of the binding of cation and melibiose is the core symport mechanism in MelBSt.
source: To understand how the sugar substrate and the coupling cations dictate transporter function, we have established thermodynamic binding cycles in MelBSt using isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) measurements and identified that the positive cooperativity of the binding of cation and melibiose as the core symport mechanism (Hariharan and Guan, 2017); furthermore, the binding of the second substrate changes the thermodynamic feature of heat capacity change from positive to negative, suggesting primary dehydration processes when both substrates concurrently occupy the transporter (Hariharan and Guan, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The binding of the second substrate changes the thermodynamic feature of heat capacity change from positive to negative in MelBSt.

evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The change in heat capacity suggests primary dehydration processes when both substrates concurrently occupy the transporter.
source: To understand how the sugar substrate and the coupling cations dictate transporter function, we have established thermodynamic binding cycles in MelBSt using isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) measurements and identified that the positive cooperativity of the binding of cation and melibiose as the core symport mechanism (Hariharan and Guan, 2017); furthermore, the binding of the second substrate changes the thermodynamic feature of heat capacity change from positive to negative, suggesting primary dehydration processes when both substrates concurrently occupy the transporter (Hariharan and Guan, 2021).
evidence: This is an interpretation of thermodynamic data.

claim: The heat capacity change may be related to forming an occluded intermediate conformation, a necessary state for a global conformational transition.
source: While the structural origins have not yet been completely determined yet, they may be related to forming an occluded intermediate conformation, a necessary state for a global conformational transition.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the structural basis of the thermodynamic observations.
